summary:
Project Summary – clean orbit 

clean orbit is an environmental monitoring and air purification project designed to address air pollution using technology and scientific data. We analyzed NASA Earth observation datasets to compare air pollution trends in Shubra El-Kheima between 2024 and 2026, identifying changes in environmental conditions over time.

The project also includes an Arduino-based system equipped with MQ-135 gas sensors to monitor air quality before and after filtration. An activated carbon filter is used to help reduce air pollutants, while the sensors measure air quality on both sides to evaluate the filtration process.

By combining NASA data analysis with real-time sensor measurements, ATMOSYNC connects environmental research with a practical solution. Our goal is to raise awareness, support data-driven environmental decisions, and contribute to creating cleaner and healthier air.
details: Project Details – ATMOSYNC ATMOSYNC is an innovative environmental project that combines NASA satellite data analysis, air quality monitoring, and air filtration to address the challenge of air pollution. How Does It Work? Our project has two main components: 1. Environmental Data Analysis: We used NASA Earth observation datasets to study and compare air pollution indicators in Shubra El-Kheima, Egypt, between 2024 and 2026. This helped us understand environmental changes and identify pollution trends over time. 2. Smart Air Monitoring and Filtration System: We developed a prototype using an Arduino Uno and two MQ-135 gas sensors. One sensor measures air quality before filtration, while the other measures it after passing through an activated carbon filter. The readings are displayed on a screen to help evaluate the filtration performance. Benefits and Expected Impact Clean orbit aims to demonstrate how technology can help monitor air pollution and reduce certain airborne pollutants. It provides a practical way to compare air quality before and after filtration, raises environmental awareness, and encourages data-driven solutions for cleaner air. Tools and Technologies - Arduino Uno for controlling the system. - Two MQ-135 sensors for air quality monitoring. - Activated carbon as a filtration material. - LCD display for showing sensor readings. - NASA Earth observation datasets for environmental analysis. - Arduino IDE and C++ for programming. - Data analysis and visualization tools for comparing environmental data. Creative Aspect The innovative aspect of clean orbit is combining large-scale satellite observations with a small, practical air filtration prototype. Instead of relying only on theoretical research, we connected environmental data with real-time measurements in a physical model. Factors Considered Our team considered the reliability of data, sensor limitations, filtration effectiveness, prototype cost, accessibility of materials, and the importance of comparing measurements under similar conditions. Our ultimate goal is to turn environmental data into practical action and inspire innovative solutions for healthier communities.
